question: Permissions for unattended agents. Which mode should the manager and specialists run in: dontAsk (anything not pre-approved is refused), auto (a classifier reviews each action), or bypassPermissions (nothing asked, nothing refused)? And for specialists: may they run arbitrary shell commands inside their copy, install packages (uv, pip, npm) into the workspace environment, and push branches to the skills' private GitHub remotes, or must every push go through the manager?

The original draft gave the manager Notes (one-off detail) and Memories (a condensed running log). The spec now has a notes folder that persists, and per-round history archived into round folders. Should Memories survive as its own thing, for example a short condensed summary the manager rewrites at the end of each round and reads at the start of the next, or is it fully replaced by the round archive?

Amalgamation proposal: inbox requests that name the same skill and the same need merge into one work folder; vector-search suggests likely matches, the manager confirms each merge, and every source request is kept with its details appended rather than rewritten. Accept as written, or change it?
Should the manager ever start a round by itself? If so, on what trigger: a number of unread inbox requests, a schedule, the watcher finding nothing active, or only when you or the host agent says so?

Constant rules can never be removed or modified. Which should be constant from day one? Candidates: the scope rule (an agent controls only its home folder), no instance ratifies its own request, tests gate every merge, acceptance tests are hidden from implementers, no always-loaded instruction files. Add or remove.
When mirroring finds that a host skill and Adapt's own copy of it have conflicting changes, which side wins by default: the host's copy, Adapt's copy, or neither until the manager decides?

Nested Adapt: should there be a depth limit, for example one Adapt inside another and no deeper? And does an inner Adapt report to the outer manager the way a host agent does, through the inbox and return files?

META TOOLS: should it be a real folder at the workspace root, as in the original draft, with the skill specialists preload being a thin pointer to it? Or should its folder under .claude/skills be the only home for the tools?

Private GitHub remotes for skills: one remote per skill-and-project pair, or one remote per skill with a branch per host project? Branches make later reconciliation across projects easier; separate remotes keep each project's copy completely apart.

What counts as a stalled round, and how should you be told? Candidates: no record written for 20 minutes, the launcher exiting with an error, or a round ending with its work item still open. Notice by a Windows desktop notification, a line in the viewer, or both?
When two specialists need to change the same file, should the manager run them one after the other, or let both work and require the second to rebase onto the first before its merge?

Documentation Dogma now applies only to manager and specialist rules and their documents. Its rule 3 says 'you can never have too few details'. Did you mean too many? And may rules 1 and 2 simply point at the existing writing rules, fact-ownership and compressed-register, instead of restating them?
